title: Some Symmetric Sign Patterns Requiring Full $P$-vertices
summary: A sign pattern is a matrix whose entries belong to $\{+, -, 0\}$. Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a symmetric sign pattern and $A$ a real symmetric matrix in its qualitative class. A vertex $v_j$ of the underlying graph of $\mathcal{P}$ is called a $P$-vertex if $ m_{A(j)}(0)-m_A(0)=1,$ where $A(j)$ is the principal submatrix obtained by deleting the $j$-th row and column of $A$, and $m_A(0), ~m_{A(j)}(0)$ denotes the algebraic multiplicity of the eigenvalue $0$ of $A, ~A(j)$, respectively.
